purpose: Mandatory win-side analysis (Phase 3.5 brief section 5) -- a failure model built from losses alone would be biased. This checks whether our strategy was actually superior in wins, or the opponent simply failed to scale/execute.
method: Same daily-trajectory extraction (results/phase3_5/trajectories/) applied to all 8 real wins, cross-referenced against results/phase3_5/differential_summary.json.
finding: In ALL 8 wins, our own resource commitment (hands=2, animals=1-2, land=1, ~21-22 MELON tiles) is essentially IDENTICAL to our commitment in the 10 losses -- we did not play differently in wins. The difference is entirely on the OPPONENT'S side: mean opp_hands_final=1.62 and opp_animals_final=0.12 in wins vs. 5.9/6.2 in losses. In 6 of 8 wins, the opponent finished with ZERO hired hands and ZERO animals (matching the 'conservative'-style low-footprint profile Phase 3.1's synthetic archetypes already cover). In the remaining 2 wins (104568456 vs Tanjim Ahmed Kingshu, 104597919 vs Shoroogh Ahmadi), the opponent DID sustain a high hand count (8 and 7 respectively) but still ended with low final money (~$1.6k-9.9k) -- their labor was not converted into comparable revenue, i.e. a high resource commitment alone is not sufficient without effective production/selling execution.
conclusion: Our wins are NOT evidence that our strategy is competitively strong or adaptive -- they are wins by DEFAULT against opponents who either stayed passive/low-footprint, or scaled labor without converting it to revenue. This is consistent with (not contradicting) the loss-side finding: our strategy is static and non-adaptive; it wins when the opponent is also static/weak, and loses when the opponent successfully scales. This is exactly why the Phase 3.5 countermeasure targets OPPONENT SCALING specifically, rather than assuming our own execution needs to change.
